name: Ibufenac

own_problems.text: Pulled from the market in United Kingdom, first in 1968 — for liver harm

similar.name: Ibuprofen
problems: Carries a boxed warning in United States — for stomach and gut problems, nerve and brain harm and heart harm

similar.name: Amphetamine
problems: Carries a boxed warning in United States — for misuse or addiction and heart harm

similar.name: Melphalan
problems: Carries a boxed warning in United States — for immune system problems and blood problems

summary: Ibufenac was removed from the market in the United Kingdom in 1968 due to liver damage [3]. A small computer model, rather than tests on people, calculated low risk scores of 30 for liver harm and 10 for heart harm [M]. Similar drugs have severe warnings in the United States, including Ibuprofen for stomach, nerve, and heart damage, Amphetamine for misuse and heart harm, and Melphalan for immune and blood-related harm [4][5][6].
